title: Building Scalable Multi-Agent AI Systems
description: Engineered MLP, CNN, LSTM, and Transformer architectures in PyTorch achieving 94.3% accuracy on MNIST and 89.1% on IMDB. Built production-grade RAG and ReAct agents using LangGraph and LangChain with locally hosted LLMs. Achieved 3.2× inference speed-up via GGUF quantization and ONNX optimization.

detail.overview:
Deep learning architectures built from scratch in PyTorch:
- MLP, CNN, LSTM, Transformer: 94.3% accuracy on MNIST, 89.1% on IMDB sentiment
- Trained end-to-end; learned low-level PyTorch internals (custom training loops, loss functions, optimizers)

Production AI agents:
- RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline: document ingestion → vector store → retrieval → generation
- ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) agents: LangGraph orchestration, LangChain tool integration, locally-hosted open-source LLMs
- Both deployed as working systems, not just notebooks
detail.implementation:
Inference optimization:
- 3.2× speed-up via GGUF quantization (reduced model size for CPU/edge inference)
- ONNX export for cross-platform, cross-framework deployment
detail.results: 94.3% accuracy on MNIST, 89.1% on IMDB sentiment. 3.2× inference speed-up via GGUF quantization and ONNX optimization.
detail.techStack: PyTorch, LangGraph, LangChain, ONNX, GGUF, Python

title: Cancer Omics Research
description: Computational biology research at IIT Bombay applying machine learning to genomic data to identify patterns in cancer omics datasets. Using ML to make sense of high-dimensional biological signals.

detail.overview:
Computational biology research at IIT Bombay applying machine learning to cancer genomics.
- Analyzing multi-omics datasets: gene expression profiles, genomic variation, and proteomics
- Goal: identify patterns, co-expression clusters, and potential biomarkers distinguishing cancer subtypes or disease states
- Research context: IIT Bombay lab, working with real biological data where labels are sparse or noisy
detail.implementation: Core ML challenge: p >> n (features far exceed samples), requiring regularization, feature selection, and dimensionality reduction. Pipeline: preprocessing → feature engineering → model training on high-dimensional genomic representations.
detail.challenges: Unlike standard ML benchmarks, biological data has high noise, batch effects, and domain-specific preprocessing requirements: normalization methods, log-transformation, filtering low-expressed genes. Every data quality decision has biological consequences.
detail.results: Ongoing active research. Working toward identifying ML-derived biomarkers that distinguish cancer subtypes from multi-omics profiles.
detail.techStack: Python, Scanpy, scikit-learn, pandas, bioinformatics preprocessing tools

title: Market Regime Detection via Unsupervised Learning
description: Applied K-Means clustering and PCA dimensionality reduction to order book data, identifying 11 distinct market regimes. Achieved Silhouette Score of 0.450 and Davies-Bouldin Index of 1.227.

detail.overview:
Quantitative finance project using unsupervised ML to identify distinct market microstructure states from order book data.
- Input: bid/ask prices, depth, spread, and volume at price levels
- Pipeline: feature engineering → PCA dimensionality reduction → K-Means clustering
detail.implementation: Feature engineering on raw order book data to extract liquidity, volatility, and momentum signals. PCA applied to reduce dimensionality before clustering. K-Means used to find natural groupings in the feature space without labeled supervision.
detail.challenges: Financial data is non-stationary and regime labels are inherently unobserved. Selecting the right number of clusters required iterating over multiple metrics and validating that discovered regimes had economic interpretability.
detail.results: 11 distinct market regimes identified, representing states such as trending, range-bound, high-volatility, and illiquid conditions. Silhouette Score: 0.450 (reasonable separation). Davies-Bouldin Index: 1.227 (competitive for financial data).
detail.techStack: Python, scikit-learn, K-Means, PCA, pandas, time-series feature engineering

title: Real-Time Object Detection & Facial Recognition
description: Deployed YOLOv8 for real-time multi-class object detection on live video streams. Implemented Siamese Neural Networks for one-shot facial recognition with high inter-class discriminability.

detail.overview: Two computer vision systems combined into one project: real-time multi-class object detection and one-shot facial recognition.
detail.implementation:
Object detection: deployed YOLOv8 (single-stage detector) for real-time multi-class detection on live video streams. Optimized for throughput.

Facial recognition: implemented Siamese Neural Networks for metric learning. One-shot approach means a face can be recognized from a single reference image without retraining. Learns a similarity/distance metric rather than fixed class labels, making it practical for open-set recognition where new identities can be added at any time.
detail.results: Real-time multi-class object detection on live video. High inter-class discriminability in facial recognition with one-shot generalization to unseen identities.
detail.techStack: PyTorch, YOLOv8, Siamese Neural Networks, OpenCV, Python

title: Gesture-Based Text Creation & Recognition
description: Built CNN in TensorFlow for handwritten MNIST digit recognition with 89%+ accuracy. Integrated MediaPipe hand-landmark detection with OpenCV for a real-time gesture-controlled drawing canvas.

detail.overview: Real-time system combining gesture tracking with handwriting recognition. Users draw digits in the air; the system recognizes them live from the camera feed.
detail.implementation:
CNN digit classifier: built in TensorFlow on MNIST, standard Conv → Pool → Dense architecture with dropout.

Gesture canvas: MediaPipe tracks 21 hand keypoints per frame from the camera. Index finger tip position draws strokes on a virtual canvas rendered by OpenCV.

Combined pipeline: camera → MediaPipe (finger tracking) → OpenCV (canvas rendering) → CNN (digit classification).
detail.results: 89%+ accuracy on handwritten digit recognition. Real-time pipeline with no perceptible lag between gesture and canvas rendering.

title: Bulldozer Price Prediction: Time Series ML
description: Trained Random Forest Regressor on 400K+ record Kaggle dataset, achieving R² = 0.88. Reduced overfitting via RandomizedSearchCV hyperparameter tuning.

detail.overview: Regression project on heavy equipment auction data (Kaggle Blue Book for Bulldozers). Predicting sale prices from 400,000+ historical auction records covering equipment specs, age, usage hours, sale date, and region.
detail.implementation:
Random Forest Regressor, robust to feature heterogeneity and nonlinear interactions.

Key decisions:
- Time-series split: validation on data strictly after training cutoff to prevent data leakage
- Feature engineering: year/month extracted from sale dates, categorical specs encoded
- Overfitting reduction: RandomizedSearchCV over n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_split
detail.challenges: Preventing data leakage in a time-series context: standard cross-validation would allow training on future data. Used a strict temporal split instead. Feature engineering required domain understanding of equipment auction specs.
detail.results: R² = 0.88, explaining 88% of auction price variance. Strong result given the noise inherent in real-world auction data.
detail.techStack: Python, scikit-learn, Random Forest, pandas, Kaggle

title: SwethankOS: 3D Retro Terminal Portfolio
description: An earlier portfolio reimagined as a fictional OS. Click a 3D laptop to boot into a CRT terminal desktop with draggable windows, a typed command-line interface, embedded mini-games, and full post-processing visual effects.

detail.overview:
An earlier personal portfolio reimagined as a fully interactive 3D retro operating system. Visitors click a Blender-modeled, Three.js-rendered laptop to trigger a CRT boot sequence, which transitions into a draggable-window desktop environment.

The centerpiece is a typed terminal with a custom command registry (about, skills, projects, contact, and more), command history, and tab-style autocomplete. The desktop includes a z-index window manager, CRT-flicker dock, ambient sound, and two embedded mini-games: Snake and a finance-themed NeuroTrade game built with Chart.js.
detail.implementation:
Notable engineering decisions:
- Z-index stacking system: a custom manager assigns z-index values so multiple draggable windows can be brought to front independently, like a real OS
- Command history as a linked list: HistoryNode class with prev/next pointers for up/down arrow traversal — a deliberate data structure choice over a plain array
- Boot progress tied to real asset loading: the CRT boot bar is wired to drei's useProgress, tracking actual .glb model load progress rather than a fake timer
- Adaptive rendering: device pixel ratio, shadows, and post-processing conditionally disabled on mobile to avoid overloading weaker GPUs
detail.challenges: Building an OS-like window manager in the browser: z-index stacking, drag behavior, and focus management across multiple simultaneous windows. Keeping 3D rendering performant while running post-processing effects. The experience is intentionally desktop-only, with a styled fallback for mobile.
detail.results: Fully interactive 3D portfolio with a working terminal CLI, two embedded mini-games, and full CRT post-processing (scanlines, noise, vignette, glitch/anaglyph mode).
detail.techStack: Three.js, React Three Fiber, @react-three/drei, @react-three/postprocessing, Blender, Framer Motion, Chart.js, Vite, React 19
